## Short answer
Growth in FY2024-25 was financed mainly by borrowings, not equity: short-term borrowings rose to ₹1,483.29 lakhs from ₹829.89 lakhs and long-term borrowings to ₹483.35 lakhs from ₹117.13 lakhs, while paid-up capital rose to ₹1,320.00 lakhs from ₹165.00 lakhs via a 1:7 bonus issue rather than a cash IPO [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.70][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.73]. Receivables quality deteriorated sharply: trade receivables jumped to ₹2,177.41 lakhs from ₹1,219.65 lakhs, with ₹96.26 lakhs over 1 year and ₹38.63 lakhs over 2 years in the 2025 ageing [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.76]. Liquidity is stretched by working-capital debt, though the auditor saw no going-concern or cash-loss issue [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.66][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.74].

## Financing of growth
- Short-term borrowings ₹1,483.29 lakhs at 31.03.2025 vs ₹829.89 lakhs at 31.03.2024, including demand loans from banks (secured) ₹1,170.88 lakhs, others (secured) ₹185.94 lakhs and current maturities of long-term borrowings ₹126.47 lakhs [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.70][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.74].
- Long-term borrowings ₹483.35 lakhs vs ₹117.13 lakhs, comprising secured bank term loans (ICICI vehicle loans, Union Bank solar loan, SIDBI ₹440.50 lakhs); unsecured director/relative loans nil at year end versus ₹82.72 lakhs prior [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.74].
- Bank facilities include a ₹1,000 lakh ICICI cash-credit limit at repo plus 2.5%, a ₹200 lakh Indian Bank overdraft at 9.75%, and a Yes Bank working-capital demand loan at 10.25% [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.74][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.75].
- Equity increase was a bonus issue of 1,15,50,000 shares; paid-up capital ₹1,320.00 lakhs (1,32,00,000 shares of ₹10) [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.73]. No IPO proceeds were raised during the year [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.65].
- Debt-equity ratio 0.94 vs 0.89 [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.81][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.41].

## Receivables quality and working capital
- Trade receivables ageing at 31.03.2025: ₹1,997.61 lakhs under 6 months, ₹96.26 lakhs 1-2 years, ₹38.63 lakhs 2-3 years, ₹8.79 lakhs over 3 years; total ₹2,177.41 lakhs, all undisputed [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.76].
- Trade receivable turnover fell to 1.62 from 9.68, an 83.26% decline attributed to increased receivables [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.81][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.41].
- Inventories ₹981.42 lakhs vs ₹829.20 lakhs; cash and bank ₹276.50 lakhs vs ₹28.14 lakhs; current ratio 1.59 vs 1.55 [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.70][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.76][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.81].
- Quarterly stock/debtor statements filed with banks did not agree with books, with variations up to ~₹307.58 lakhs attributed to timing and clerical errors [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.80][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.64].

## Growth and profitability
- Revenue from operations ₹11,011.18 lakhs vs ₹8,139.32 lakhs; total income ₹110,69,33,000 vs ₹83,27,48,000 [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.40][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.20].
- Profit after tax ₹1,014.93 lakhs vs ₹501.79 lakhs; PBT ₹1,385.51 lakhs vs ₹676.65 lakhs [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.5][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.20][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.72].

## Cash flow and auditor view
- Net cash from operating activities ₹444.43 lakhs vs ₹271.58 lakhs, after working-capital outflow driven by receivables of ₹957.75 lakhs [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.72].
- Financing inflow ₹248.36 lakhs, with proceeds from short-term borrowings ₹741.85 lakhs and long-term borrowings ₹366.22 lakhs, partly offset by finance costs paid ₹277.77 lakhs [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.72].
- Auditors reported no qualification or adverse remark, no cash losses in the year or prior year, and no material uncertainty on going concern; liabilities expected to be met within one year [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.29][Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.66].
- The company has not defaulted in repayment of loans or borrowings [Bhadora Industries Annual Report p.65].

GREETINGS!! It gives me immense pleasure to welcome you all to the 12th Annual General Meeting of Bhadora Industries Limited (Vidhut Cables). On behalf of the Board of Directors, I extend my heartfelt gratitude for your continued support, trust, and encouragement that has enabled our Company to progress with strength and resilience. I am delighted to share with you the highlights of our Company’s performance for the financial year 2024–25. Despite a highly competitive and challenging environment, Bhadora Industries Limited achieved a revenue of₹11,011.18 lakhs, reflecting the strength of our business model and the commitment of our people. Further, we recorded a net profit of ₹1,014.93 lakhs, a testimony to our operational efficiency, disciplined cost management, and value creation for our stakeholders. This year also marks a significant milestone in the journey of Bhadora Industries Limited on August 11, 2025, our Company was successfully listed on the Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Exchange. This achievement is not just a recognition of our consistent performance, but also a gateway to new opportunities, enhanced visibility, and greater access to capital markets. I take this moment to thank all our shareholders, employees, bankers, advisors, and well-wishers who played a vital role in making this possible.
